dominant_strengths: Comprehensive granular consent options exposed inline rather than buried, giving users actual control over each tracking purpose
Clear binary Disagree/Agree pairing per row makes the decision model legible and consistent throughout the long list
dominant_weaknesses: Generic Didomi template with zero Nothing brand expression—no dot-matrix type, monochrome rigor, or signature visual identity present at all
Aggressive green Agree buttons versus neutral Disagree creates dark-pattern asymmetry, undermining the consent-as-choice premise
Dense 14-row wall of '+' toggles with cramped spacing produces fatigue and decision paralysis rather than calm scannability
fix_priorities: Rebrand entirely in Nothing's monochrome dot-matrix system—replace green CTAs with equal-weight black/white toggle pairs
Collapse the 14 purposes into 3-4 grouped categories with progressive disclosure to reduce cognitive load
Equalize visual weight between Agree and Disagree to remove coercive bias and align with ethical consent design
Introduce structural rhythm (dividers, generous vertical spacing, typographic hierarchy) so the list breathes
rationale.norman_balance: Behavioral function works mechanically but visceral appeal is absent and reflective trust is damaged by the green-button bias.
rationale.intent_fit: This is a stock third-party consent modal with no Nothing-phone design language whatsoever, so it fails the brand brief almost entirely.
